name: Fog-broom grass (living)
description: The fog-broom grass Stipagrostis sabulicola - the plant that makes the oasis. Its fan of grooved leaves condenses ocean fog into droplets (up to 39 mm a year, more than the rainfall) that water a hidden arthropod community in the leaf axils. This node is the living foliage: the source's 'fresh leaves' basal pool, tapped for sap by the scale insects and leafhoppers living under the sheaths. Species node matching the source's fresh-leaves basal pool.
